A regular milling machine will suffice quite well if one can read the blueprints. Harborfreight sells a serviceable machine. Caveat, I have not used the smaller HF 'benchtop' machine. Craigslist can also have old milling machines, most of which are better than a HF special. I have seen some screaming deals. There are older books which detail how to make a whole machine shop with a milling machine. You can also get milling table for a lathe or get a heavy duty drill press and turn it into a milling machine, like here. Which in conjunction with some casting ability, be used to make a better milling machine. Though for all the hours involved, buying one would be better. Lurk on some machining forums to get a lot of good information, maybe here. There is also this guy who cast and then machined a lower. Though it'd be better to start with a 6061 or 7075 blank unless I had to. 6061 vs 7075 is a whole other can of worms, but likely won't matter for most. I guess old scuba tanks could be a good place to get 6061. Breaking down airplane parts could be much harder. I think I'd just cast bricks after seeing issues with going for complex casting with cores. Either way casting is a PITA.
